title: Choose the institutional Helios workbench
question: Synchronized Evidence Desk is my recommendation. It keeps the complete OMS lifecycle legible while making Helios ownable through one shared event-time surface for market, signal, source, risk, order, fill, and portfolio evidence.

options.label: Synchronized Evidence Desk
options.lineage: institutional blotters, scientific trace review, and point-in-time decision evidence
options.thesis: Every decision is a place on one shared timeline, with the exact observations, order state, and downstream result available for inspection.
options.viewport: A dominant synchronized timeline stacks selectable market, posterior, source-quality, risk, and P&L series under one crosshair. Order, acknowledgement, fill, cancel, replace, and alert markers share the same event-time axis. A working-order ledger below carries parent and child state, route, owner, allocation, compliance, reconciliation, and last event. The evidence rail explains a selected interval from cited observations.
options.case: This is the best synthesis of the product. It supports ordinary OMS work without hiding Helios's differentiator: causal, replayable, point-in-time investigation across research and execution.
options.risk: A large timeline can crowd the blotter on smaller screens, so mobile and narrow desktop modes must preserve the shared cursor while moving ledger and evidence detail into explicit panes.

raised.raise: Parent and child orders, fills, allocations, compliance, exceptions, reconciliation, post-trade, TCA, and audit remain first-class destinations.
AI assembles cited evidence and suggests relevant series, but stays read-only and cannot bypass risk or command review.

options.label: Graphite Order Record
options.lineage: Charles River Trader, Bloomberg AIM, Trading Technologies, and high-density execution ledgers
options.thesis: The order is the primary record; every lifecycle transition, break, and post-trade obligation remains visible around it.
options.viewport: A large grouped parent and child blotter owns the center. A shallow synchronized market chart places order, cancel, replace, and fill markers above it; an exception rail separates compliance, venue uncertainty, allocation, and reconciliation breaks; fills, allocations, audit, and TCA live in a docked detail record.
options.case: This is the safest institutional choice and the clearest for a trading desk adopting Helios as a standalone OMS or overlaying an existing one.
options.risk: It can over-index on order handling and make signal research feel secondary unless the evidence timeline is promoted into a peer workspace.

raised.raise: It preserves conventional order hierarchy but removes generic KPI cards and exposes the full exception surface.

options.label: Market Evidence Atlas
options.lineage: multi-track observability, point-in-time research notebooks, and execution replay
options.thesis: Operators compose the evidence field itself, stacking any market, model, source, portfolio, or execution series against a common clock.
options.viewport: A majestic configurable analysis surface stacks price, spread, volume, signal strength, posterior probability, latency, exposure, capacity, and P&L. The operator scrubs one interval across order and fill ribbons. The evidence rail distinguishes what was available at decision time from late arrivals, then offers cited investigation and operator-approved series suggestions.
options.case: This is the most visually ownable and the strongest quant-research workspace. It makes AI-native investigation useful without turning the product into a chatbot.
options.risk: It is not sufficient as the only home surface. Orders, allocations, compliance, reconciliation, and audit still need dedicated lifecycle workspaces with equivalent depth.

raised.raise: More traces fit at once and selected intervals expose late-arrival and model-version truth directly.

canonCard.label: Conventional Institutional OMS
canonCard.thesis: The familiar dark enterprise OMS executed against the functional bar set by Charles River Trader, Bloomberg AIM, and Trading Technologies.
canonCard.viewport: A collapsible sidebar, portfolio summary, working-order blotter, positions, source health, and alert center. Standard operations are legible, but time-series evidence remains a secondary chart rather than the organizing model.
canonCard.risk: Reliable and easy to recognize, but too easy to mistake for any other polished institutional product and too weak at point-in-time causal investigation.
